newsitem.title: JAPAN: MITI welcomes TEPCO's plan to cut rates.
newsitem.headline: MITI welcomes TEPCO's plan to cut rates.

text.p: Japan's trade minister on Friday welcomed a decision by Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc (TEPCO) to cut electricity rates some time early next year.
"(TEPCO's plans) can be praised as a first step in the direction of ongoing economic structure reforms," Shinji Sato, Minister for International Trade and Industry said in a statement.
Sato also said he hoped that other electric power utilities would follow TEPCO's decision swiftly.
TEPCO president Hiroshi Araki told a news conference on Friday that the company plans to reduce electricity prices early next year but did not specify the exact date or extent of the cut.
"We believe, as a result of our cost-cutting efforts, our financial situation is healthy enough to endure the price cut," he said.

The Japanese government said last December it aims to bring Japan's electricity prices into line with international levels by 2001 as part of a wider programme to promote Japan's economic structural reform.
Araki spoke ahead of the release by the government later this month of a detailed action plan to carry out the programme.
Industry estimates show that the average family in Japan pays about 20 percent more for its electricity than a German family and 30 percent more than a family in the United States.
